title: [epic] Kill desktop-responsive branch — fold desktop layout into main, build /d/ from main
description:
STRUCTURAL FIX subsuming three problems:

1. Message history doesn't render in /d/ (user-reported, 2026-06-01)
2. desktop-responsive branch is ~20+ commits behind main (last sync OpenChat-on1 on 2026-05-31). 22+ files/screens on main don't exist on desktop-responsive: agent keys, MCP snippets, voice messages, link previews, Thoughts stream, transforms, forwarding, ContactProfile, ChatEmptyState, blocked users, group invites, OpenChat home page link.
3. Manual merge work each release with hand-conflict ChatPane.tsx refactor.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
GEMINI SECOND OPINION + CODEX INDEPENDENT REVIEW (both 2026-06-01)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Saved at ~/memory/research/2026-06-01-gemini-openchat-desktop-fold-review.md
       and ~/memory/research/2026-06-01-codex-openchat-d-fold-review.md

REVISED APPROACH (Gemini + Codex):

═══ STRUCTURAL ═══

1. **Screen-level responsive routing (Gemini) — NOT top-level shell swap.**
   ❌ Original: return isDesktop ? <DesktopShell /> : <MobileShell /> in App.tsx → would unmount NavigationContainer, lose nav state + composer text + scroll + navigationRef.
   ✅ Fix: ONE NavigationContainer. Responsive swap inside individual SCREENS.

2. **Preserve main's bottom-tab architecture (Codex).**
   Main's current shape: RootStack → AuthedTabs → ChatsNavigator → ThoughtsNavigator.
   Desktop branch is from BEFORE this nested-tab refactor — porting requires implementing the responsive swap INSIDE the bottom-tab structure, not replacing it.
   ✅ In App.tsx: keep RootStack, AuthedTabs, ChatsNavigator, ThoughtsNavigator.
   ✅ Change only ChatsNavigator stack: ConversationsScreen → HomeScreen, ChatScreen → ChatScreenRouter.

3. **Use .web.tsx file extensions (Gemini) — NOT Platform.OS gates with React.lazy.**
   Metro compile-time resolves → 0 KB native bundle bloat.

4. **CRITICAL: every .web.tsx imported by shared code MUST have a native shim (Codex).**
   If App.tsx imports HomeScreen and only HomeScreen.web.tsx exists, iOS build fails.
   Required FILE PAIRS:
   - src/screens/HomeScreen.tsx (native: re-export ConversationsScreen)
   - src/screens/HomeScreen.web.tsx (responsive: useIsDesktop() → MasterDetailLayout vs ConversationsScreen)
   - src/screens/ChatScreenRouter.tsx (native: re-export ChatScreen)
   - src/screens/ChatScreenRouter.web.tsx (responsive: master-detail aware)
   - src/components/MasterDetailLayout.web.tsx (web-only, imported only from .web.tsx)
   - src/components/ChatPane.web.tsx (web-only)
   - src/components/ConversationList.web.tsx (web-only)
   - src/components/MaxWidthContent.web.tsx (web-only, narrow CSS-only impact)
   - src/screens/KeyboardShortcutsScreen.web.tsx (web-only, imported only by .web.tsx)
   - src/theme/breakpoints.ts (shared hook useIsDesktop)

5. **app.config.js for env-driven baseUrl, GUARDED for web only (Gemini).**
   const baseUrl = process.env.OPENCHAT_BASE_URL || undefined;
   experiments: { baseUrl: process.env.IS_WEB_BUILD ? baseUrl : undefined }
   Setting baseUrl on iOS / Android corrupts deep links + asset mapping.

6. **Breakpoint: 900px** (Gemini, confirmed).

═══ DEPLOY PIPELINE (Codex) ═══

7. **CRITICAL: distinct output dirs + inline env per command — NO leakage.**
   IS_WEB_BUILD=1 OPENCHAT_BASE_URL=/m npx expo export --platform web --output-dir dist-web-m --clear
   IS_WEB_BUILD=1 OPENCHAT_BASE_URL=/d npx expo export --platform web --output-dir dist-web-d --clear
   Then copy dist-web-m/ → client-mobile/dist/, dist-web-d/ → client-mobile-desktop/dist/.
   Add validator: grep '/m/' in client-mobile/dist/index.html (must hit), grep '/d/' must MISS. And vice versa for desktop. Fail deploy if cross-contamination.

═══ MERGE TIMING (Codex) ═══

8. **DO NOT MERGE TO main DURING TestFlight train.**
   Build 36 (v0.1.4) is currently in EAS auto-submit. 601 touches app.config.js, navigation/types.ts, route mappings, and several screens. Native EAS builds from main could break mid-train.
   - Work on a separate branch + worktree (~/.omnara/worktrees/openchat-mobile/<name>) NOW
   - WAIT until build 36 is visible in TestFlight
   - Pause new automatic native builds during the transition
   - After 601 lands, run ONE deliberate native EAS build as build 37 to verify

═══ ROOT CAUSE OF /d/ MESSAGE-HISTORY BUG (Gemini, verified) ═══

- desktop-ChatContext.tsx (lines 343-347): api.getMessages(id).then(msgs => setMessages(msgs))
- main-ChatContext.tsx (lines 527-531): api.getMessages(id).then(({ messages: msgs, hasMore }) => { setMessages(msgs); setHasMoreMessages(hasMore); })
- Main introduced pagination (OpenChat-vjc) that changed the API response shape from raw array to { messages, hasMore }. Desktop still expects array → setMessages(non-array) → 'prev.some is not a function' or empty render.
- Folding /d/ to main code automatically fixes this. NO manual patch needed.

═══ ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ═══

- [ ] /m/ unchanged — login, message history, all features work
- [ ] /d/ runs from main with /d/ baseUrl — master-detail, sidebar collapse, Cmd-K + Cmd-N work
- [ ] /d/ message history renders (original bug, fixed as side-effect)
- [ ] /d/ has all post-OpenChat-on1 features: agent keys, MCP card, voice, link previews, thoughts, transforms, forwarding, contact profile, etc.
- [ ] iOS TestFlight build 37 passes — .web.tsx ensures 0 KB desktop code in native bundle
- [ ] Native shim files exist for every .web.tsx imported from shared code
- [ ] Push-notification deep-link tap works on iOS through the nested tab → stack structure
- [ ] Push-notification deep-link tap works on /m/ and /d/ web
- [ ] desktop-responsive branch deleted locally + on GitHub (after merge to main)
- [ ] deploy.sh simplified — single openchat-mobile checkout, two exports with isolated output dirs + cross-contamination validator
- [ ] Browser-resize between mobile and desktop widths does NOT remount NavigationContainer or lose composer text
- [ ] npx tsc --noEmit clean
- [ ] Bundle-size delta documented in close-reason

═══ FOLLOW-UPS ═══

- Close OpenChat-74g as 'subsumed by OpenChat-601' AFTER confirming react-dom, react-native-web, @expo/metro-runtime remain in package.json
- 601.1 (back-to-home affordance in /d/) is a child task; lands after 601 master-detail is on main
- 3rw (PWA) waits for 601 to ship and stabilize

ESTIMATED EFFORT: 4–5 hours focused on separate branch. Merge to main only after TestFlight build 36 is confirmed visible.

Decision 2026-06-01: keep the existing clientLogger.ts → /api/client-logs pipeline as our crash reporter. Sentry deferred until paying-customer demand.

EXISTING REPORTING (verified working in builds 32-38):
- openchat-mobile/src/services/clientLogger.ts:
  * Hooks ErrorUtils.setGlobalHandler (uncaught native exceptions)
  * Hooks globalThis 'unhandledrejection' (unhandled promise rejections)
  * Batches POST to /api/client-logs every 1s, immediate flush on errors
  * Queue capped at 200, drops oldest on overrun (no recursion)
- openchat/server/src/routes/clientLogs.ts:
  * Rate-limited (120/min/IP)
  * Logs JSON-structured entries to stdout

PREVIOUS SENTRY ATTEMPT (build 29 commit 5ac04f1, version 6.7.x):
Failed with C++ compile error in @sentry/react-native's iOS native module. Symptom: 'std::allocator does not support const types'. Removed entirely; crashReporting.ts left as a no-op wrapper for future re-enable.

WHY NOT RE-TRY SENTRY NOW:
- Current scale (~10 testers): docker logs grep is sufficient
- Risk: a Sentry SDK upgrade (currently 8.13.x; previous attempt was 6.7.x) could regress the iOS build mid-TestFlight train — would block OpenChat-601's just-shipped builds
- Cost-benefit: paid Sentry tier ($26/mo) for symbolication, breadcrumbs, releases — not worth it pre-revenue
- Alternative: when we DO want professional crash reporting, the path is (a) test Sentry 8.13.x in a separate worktree, (b) verify native build via EAS, (c) only then merge to main

title: [P0] Account deletion (App Store 5.1.1(v))
description:
Apple has required in-app account deletion since 2022. Apple WILL REJECT the next submission without this.

CODEX REVIEW REVISION (2026-05-31): Apple's account-deletion guidance is stricter than 'anonymize'. Per https://developer.apple.com/support/offering-account-deletion-in-your-app/ users expect their UGC to actually be deleted. Recommended implementation:
- Hard-delete: User node + tokens + push subs + media uploads
- For messages: REPLACE the body with 'Message deleted' (NOT anonymize-with-sender-name). This preserves conversation structure but removes content that could identify the deleted user.
- This is safer under GDPR Recital 26 (true non-identifiability) and CCPA deletion rights.

SERVER:
- DELETE /api/auth/me endpoint
- Wipes: User node, owned Conversations (or remove participation if shared), NativePushToken, sessions/refresh-tokens, uploaded media
- For all of the user's messages: UPDATE content='Message deleted', editedAt=now, senderName='Former user'
- Cascade revocation of any OAuth grants

MOBILE:

- Confirmation modal with typed 'DELETE' confirmation
- POST DELETE /api/auth/me, then signOut()
- After: cannot sign back in with same email (or: re-signup creates a new fresh account)

AC: account deletion completes in <5s; reopening app returns to Login; other participants see 'Message deleted' placeholders where the user's messages were; no media or sender info remains.

title: [P1] Self-serve agent API keys — seamless 'connect your bot' onboarding
description:
Make it dead simple for anyone (Jacob, a user, a friend) to plug their own agent/bot into OpenChat. Today picortex uses a one-off out-of-band JWT minted by a developer. We need a self-serve API key flow with re-viewable keys (NOT one-time-view), provenance fields, scopes, and a working MCP surface.

GOOD PRACTICES TO INHERIT FROM world-issue-tracker + wikihub:

1. **Prefix convention**: keys start with 'oc_' (parallels 'wh_' / 'wit_'). First 12 chars are the visible 'key prefix' used for UI display, full key only visible when retrieved.
2. **Standard Bearer auth**: 'Authorization: Bearer oc_…' on every endpoint, not a custom X-Agent-Key header. Matches WikiHub convention (cleaner than WIT's X-Agent-Key).
3. **Provenance fields**: each key has agent_name (e.g. 'my-summary-bot') + agent_version + scopes + expires_at + last_used_at — same shape as WikiHub's ApiKey model.
4. **Scopes**: at minimum 'read' + 'write'. Future: per-conversation scoping, send-only, read-only mention listening.
5. **Credentials file convention**: agents should expect to read from ~/.openchat/credentials.json (mode 0600), parallel to ~/.wikihub/credentials.json.
6. **MCP server**: build a sibling openchat-mcp-server adapter (parallel to wikihub's mcp-server/). Tools: oc_send_message, oc_list_conversations, oc_get_messages, oc_react, oc_create_dm, oc_register_agent. Exposes both stdio + HTTP transports.

DEVIATIONS FROM WIT/WikiHub (per Jacob's explicit feedback):

7. **Keys are RE-VIEWABLE, not one-time-view**. WIT + WikiHub both show the key once at creation and store only the hash — Jacob explicitly does NOT want that. Implementation: store the FULL plaintext key in DB, encrypted at rest with a server-side KMS key (OC_KEY_ENCRYPTION_SECRET env var, rotatable separately from the database). User can re-view any of their keys from Settings → Agent Keys at any time. Threat model: DB read leaks encryption-key-encrypted blob, not plaintext.

UI:
- Settings → Agent Keys (new section)
- List existing keys: name, prefix (oc_xxxx…), last used, expiry, [View] [Revoke] buttons
- 'New key' button: prompts for name + scopes + optional expiry → returns the full key, copy-to-clipboard
- Each key row has [View full key] → reveals plaintext after Face ID / passphrase re-auth (TBD)
- Each key row has [Copy] for the agent name + key in one shot

SERVER:
- New Neo4j node: :AgentKey { id, ownerUserId, name, keyPrefix, keyEncrypted, scopes, agentName, agentVersion, expiresAt, createdAt, lastUsedAt, revokedAt }
- (User)-[:OWNS_KEY]->(AgentKey)
- POST /api/agent-keys { name, scopes?, expiresAt? } — authed; mints + returns plaintext
- GET /api/agent-keys — authed; lists keys with prefix-only (no plaintext)
- GET /api/agent-keys/:id/reveal — authed; returns full plaintext key (with audit log entry)
- PATCH /api/agent-keys/:id { name?, scopes? } — authed; rename or change scope
- DELETE /api/agent-keys/:id — authed; sets revokedAt
- New middleware resolveActor: tries JWT first, then Bearer oc_… key. Resolves to owning user. Updates lastUsedAt async.
- Picortex's JWT-based auth stays (don't break) but is grandfathered; future bots go through this.

DOCS:
- README section: 'Connect your bot in 30 seconds'
  1. Settings → Agent Keys → Create
  2. curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer oc_…' https://chat.globalbr.ai/api/chat/conversations
- openchat-mcp-server README + Cursor/Claude Desktop config snippet
- Add to landing page /about: a 'Connect your bot' link with the 30-second walkthrough

ACCEPTANCE:
- A non-technical user can sign up, get an API key, and POST a message via curl in under 2 minutes
- An MCP-aware client (Claude Desktop) can be configured with one JSON snippet to talk to OpenChat
- Keys are re-viewable from Settings indefinitely (until revoked)
- Revocation is immediate (cached resolver invalidated within 60s)
- Audit log of key reveal events

title: [mobile][bug] Chat scroll behavior: at-bottom-aware auto-scroll + new-messages pill
description:
Today: ChatScreen.tsx scrolls to bottom on EVERY message arrival, regardless of where the user is scrolled. If the user scrolled up to read history, a new message yanks them down. Real-chat-app expectation:

1. AT BOTTOM + new message arrives → smooth-scroll to keep them at the latest
2. SCROLLED UP + new message arrives → DON'T scroll. Show a floating 'N new messages ↓' pill above the composer
3. Tap pill → scroll to bottom + clear unread count
4. Reach bottom by manual scroll → clear unread count automatically
5. Own message sent → always scroll to bottom (the user is implicitly at-bottom)

Affects iOS app + RN-web /m/ + RN-web /d/. One implementation in src/screens/ChatScreen.tsx covers all three.

Pitfalls to handle correctly:
- Keyboard open/close shifts layout; ignore scroll events for ~200ms after keyboard transition OR snap to bottom if we WERE at bottom before keyboard opened
- Threshold for 'at bottom' should be ~50-100px (not 0) because RN scroll never hits exact bottom in practice
- Programmatic scrollToEnd() should still update isAtBottom correctly via onScroll
- Day separators jump contentSize between messages; use onContentSizeChange to recompute isAtBottom after content grows

Acceptance: tester sends 10 messages while scrolled up reading history; ChatScreen doesn't scroll them; pill shows '10 new messages ↓'; tapping pill scrolls to bottom + pill disappears.

- src/screens/ChatScreen.tsx — added isAtBottomRef + isAtBottom state + unreadCount; rewrote the messages.length effect to only scrollToEnd when (a) initial mount, (b) own message, or (c) user was already at bottom; added onScroll handler that computes distance-from-bottom from nativeEvent geometry; added Keyboard.keyboardDidShow listener that re-pins users who were at the bottom when the keyboard opens; reset all scroll state on conversation switch.

AT_BOTTOM_THRESHOLD_PX = 100.

title: 401 cascade: app shows error toast then strands user, no logout/refresh path
description:
When the access token expires (15min from Noos), the SPA at chat.globalbr.ai is left in a broken state:

Repro (verified live with Chrome DevTools 2026-05-30, screenshots in /tmp/openchat-04-toast-broken-no-dismiss.png):
1. Token in localStorage.openchat_token expires
2. GET /api/chat/conversations returns 401
3. ApiClient.fetch (client/src/api.ts) throws 'Invalid or expired token' — no refresh attempt, no localStorage clear, no logout, no redirect
4. ChatContext.loadConversations catch shows toast.error('Failed to load conversations') — auto-dismisses after 6s, no X button, no way to dismiss manually
5. Socket.IO useChatSocket connect_error fires with server-side Error('Invalid token') — only console.errors, perpetual 'Reconnecting...' spinner
6. User is stranded on the chat page with stale UI, no way to recover without manually clearing localStorage

Fix work is in git stash@{0}: 'stash-during-darkmode-deploy' — 6 files, ~455 insertions, codex-reviewed shape + implementation. Includes:
- Single-flight refresh via shared promise (Noos refresh tokens are rotated — would race otherwise)
- New refreshAccessToken() / clearAuth() / emitTokenRefreshed / emitAuthExpired helpers in api.ts
- 401-then-refresh-then-retry in fetch<T>() and getMe() (also fixes latent /me URL bug — was hitting /api/chat/me instead of /api/auth/me)
- Refresh-loop guard: consecutiveRefreshes counter capped at REFRESH_LOOP_LIMIT=3 (codex 2026-05-30 caught the per-effect-run flag would loop forever if every refreshed token is rejected)
- ChatProvider listens for noos:token-refreshed (updates React token state) + noos:auth-expired (clears state + navigate('/login') + toast)
- New utils/toastError.tsx component: dismissible (X button + click-anywhere + Esc), role=alert, aria-live=assertive, stable-id de-dupe (so loadConversations spam doesn't stack)
- All 10 toast.error() sites swapped to toastError() with stable IDs
- logout() now clears openchat_refresh_token (was leaking)
- register/ssoExchange now persist refreshToken (was dropping it)

Codex critique status: blessed shape + impl after addressing the refresh-loop guard. Remaining concerns are non-blocking (SSR guards in ChatProvider, possible slight double-toast on auth-expired).

title: Alice (web client) stuck in 'Reconnecting...' loop; bot doesn't reply in affected sessions
description:
Repro: Jacob signs in as Alice on chat.globalbr.ai; UI shows 'Reconnecting...' badge continuously; bot ('picortex@bot.globalbr.ai') doesn't reply in DMs even though human↔human chat appears to work.

Server logs (sudo docker logs openchat_app) show rapid connect/disconnect pairs for the same userId with different socket IDs — pattern: User connected → User disconnected within sub-second gaps. This repeats indefinitely. Not caused by the OpenChat-09h deploy — pre-existing (logs show this pattern among MULTIPLE users not just Alice).

Likely root cause: client uses transports: ['websocket', 'polling'] (see client/src/hooks/useChatSocket.ts:31). Cloudflare's proxy breaks socket.io polling fallback — the polling cycle of 'connect, XHR, close, new connect' is probably looking like real disconnects on server side. picortex bot hit the same bug and switched to transports: ['websocket']-only on 2026-04-23; fix verified empirically.

Fix to try first:
1. client/src/hooks/useChatSocket.ts: change transports to ['websocket'] only (same as picortex OpenChatChannel). If WS fails, error visibly rather than silently degrading to polling.
2. Ensure Cloudflare WebSocket upgrade is enabled for chat.globalbr.ai (should be — Noos works fine)
3. If still reconnecting: add socket.io debug logging + inspect the disconnect reason ('transport close', 'ping timeout', etc.)

Bot-not-replying angle: if user is in a DM with picortex@bot that was created BEFORE picortex-6bw / OpenChat-09h deploy, the bot should still be joined to it from picortex's 30s poll — but if the openchat socket is unstable as above, message:new broadcasts may not reach the bot either. This ticket is likely the root cause of multiple bot-not-replying reports.

title: [Bug] First message to picortex bot on a brand-new DM gets no reply (discovery race)
description:
Symptom (Jacob, 2026-04-23): DMing picortex@bot.globalbr.ai on chat.globalbr.ai for the first time, the bot does NOT reply. The SECOND message reliably gets a reply. Jacob suspected a timing issue.

Root cause: CONFIRMED — conversation-discovery race.

Evidence (replicated 2026-04-24 03:37-03:38 UTC):
- Fresh test user e2e_fresh_1777001825 creates NEW DM with bot via POST /api/chat/conversations (participantIds=['picortex_bot_...'], type='direct'). Convo id: bFh8_dWEIXwNvNEH3hwJF.
- Tester immediately sends 'FIRST msg' (message id qXVCMaK2THy3zKYZMPtUT). Broadcast via io.to('conversation:bFh8...').emit('message:new', ...). Bot is NOT in that room yet → not delivered.
- ~2s later picortex's 30s poll fires (03:37:47), sees the new convo (total 3→4), emits conversation:join, enters the room.
- Tester sends 'SECOND msg' at 03:38:00 (id 3uUODTcqrOLrrFa3cpdUb). Bot receives it and replies 2s later with 'Hey! Got your message. What can I help you with?'.
- picortex journalctl confirms: the first message id NEVER appears in logs; the second message id does. Bot-side socket only received the convo it just joined.

Root cause in code
- server/src/websocket/chatHandler.ts message:send handler (line 148): io.to('conversation:' + conversationId).emit('message:new', message). Only sockets that have previously called conversation:join are in the room.
- server/src/routes/chat.ts POST /conversations (lines 66-138): creates Conversation + PARTICIPATES_IN edges, returns 201. NO socket emit to notify the other participants that they are now in a new conversation.
- No conversation:created, conversation:new, or participant:added event exists on the socket server.
- Bot-side mitigation is a 30s poll (OpenChat-3ld: 'Periodic re-poll every 30s for newly-added conversations'), which creates a 0-30s window where the first message is silently dropped.

Proposed fix (server side — this ticket)
- In chat.ts POST /conversations: after CREATE, for each participant, io.to(<their user room / sockets>).emit('conversation:created', conversation) — or emit 'participant:added' to each participant.
- Options for addressing sockets per user: (a) have every socket join a 'user:${userId}' room on connect in chatHandler.ts, then emit io.to('user:' + participantId); (b) iterate userSockets map.
- Consider same event for 'add participant to existing conversation' flow (groups) once that UI ships — solves the same race for groups.
- Optionally: also buffer/retry the initial message:send if it finds zero room members who are actual participants — but the proper fix is the event.

Proposed fix (bot side — track via OpenChat-3ld)
- picortex listens for conversation:created / participant:added; on receipt, immediately GET conversation and emit conversation:join before any message arrives.
- Keep the 30s poll as a fallback.

Repro script
- /Users/Jacob/code/picortex/.claude/worktrees/agent-a8b9f846/scripts/e2e-openchat-new-convo.mjs
- Env: OPENCHAT_JWT_SECRET, TESTER_USER_ID, TESTER_EMAIL, BOT_USER_ID (default picortex_bot_7ecd2883dbd5ceef). Use a FRESH tester user that has no prior conversation with the bot (create in Neo4j first).
- Verdict field 'hypothesis_confirmed' prints true when first msg gets no reply and second msg does.

Related tickets
- OpenChat-3ld (picortex OpenChatChannel impl; v0.2 bullet listens for conversation:added — this is that event, needs server side)
- OpenChat-aoy (Group chats validation — same race affects adding bot to existing group)
- OpenChat-8bk (picortex bot user flow)
- OpenChat-qz0 (Add connection recovery for missed messages — related but not the same issue)

title: Real-time sidebar updates and unread message indicators
description:
**Problem:**
Two related issues with message notifications and real-time updates:

1. **Sidebar doesn't update for non-active conversations**
   - When you have conversation A open and receive a message in conversation B, the sidebar doesn't show that B has new messages
   - No unread badge/indicator appears
   - Conversation order doesn't update to show most recent at top
   - Have to click on the conversation to see there's a new message

2. **New contact messages require page refresh**
   - When someone new messages you, it doesn't appear in the conversation list
   - Must refresh the entire page to see the new conversation

**What's idiomatic in chat apps (Slack, Discord, WhatsApp, Messenger):**

1. **Unread indicators:**
   - Red dot/badge with unread count on conversations
   - Bold text for conversation name when unread
   - Preview text shows latest message

2. **Conversation list behavior:**
   - Conversations reorder in real-time (most recent at top)
   - New conversations appear automatically at top
   - Visual highlight/animation when new message arrives

3. **Real-time updates via WebSocket:**
   - Already have WebSocket for messages in active chat
   - Need to also push updates to sidebar state
   - When message received for conversation X: update X's lastMessage, lastMessageAt, unreadCount

**Implementation approach:**

1. **State management:**
   - Track unreadCount per conversation
   - Update when: message received for non-active conversation
   - Clear when: user opens that conversation

2. **WebSocket events:**
   - On new_message event: update the affected conversation in sidebar state
   - On new_conversation event: add to conversation list

3. **UI components:**
   - Add unread badge component to ConversationListItem
   - Sort conversations by lastMessageAt (descending)
   - Highlight/animate on new message

**Affects:** Core chat UX - users expect real-time updates in any modern chat app
close_reason: v1 shipped (45f9b80). Client-side unreadByConv Map in ChatContext, bumped in handleMessage when conv is non-active and sender isn't self, cleared in setActiveConversation. ConversationList renders a blue pill (99+ cap) + bolder weight for unread rows. Real-time sidebar reorder was already in place from the 401-cascade work (handleMessage re-sorts conversations on every inbound). v2 — server-side lastReadAt + cross-device sync — left as follow-up, not blocking. Stretch animation/highlight per ticket also deferred.

title: Secure SSO token exchange (don't pass JWT in URL)
description:
SECURITY: Passing JWTs in URL query parameters is a security risk.

**Current:** GET /auth/callback?token=jwt_here
URLs are logged in browser history, proxy logs, server access logs.

**Fix options:**
1. Use fragment identifier (#token=...) - not sent to server
2. Use short-lived exchange code (OAuth2 pattern) - POST to exchange for JWT
3. Use HttpOnly cookies for session management

From Gemini audit: 'Passing JWTs in URL query parameters is a security risk'
close_reason: SSO callback now prefers auth code/fragment token; JWTs are no longer required in URL query.

title: Fix contact search to use server-side API (scalability critical)
description:
CRITICAL: The frontend loads ALL contacts and filters locally. This will crash browsers at scale.

**Current behavior:**
- loadContacts() fetches all users
- Frontend filters with contacts.filter()

**Required fix:**
- Remove default 'load all' behavior
- Call API with search term: GET /api/chat/contacts?q=searchTerm
- Debounce search input (300ms)
- Show 'Type to search...' prompt instead of loading everyone

From Gemini audit: 'If Noos has 10,000 users... the Frontend loadContacts() puts all 10k objects into React State'
close_reason: Fixed in commit bb3ecd8. Frontend now uses server-side search with debouncing.

description:

title: Deploy openchat-agent on fresh GCP e2-micro (shared-bot canonical)
description:
Per OpenChat-p9y + Codex 2026-06-01 review: openchat-agent is the canonical shared-bot path. Deploy it on a fresh isolated GCP e2-micro.

## Why this host (not the alternatives)
- GCP e2-micro: ~$5/mo, fully isolated, legible security boundary
- NOT testcortex: it's on Jacob's Tailscale; agent capabilities tend to grow even if v1 has no shell tools — Codex's words. Boundary belongs before compromise, not after.
- NOT picortex-v1 co-host: defeats the isolation that justifies retiring picortex
- NOT Mac Mini: too many other services
- NOT Fly.io / Hetzner: GCP credits available; consistency with rest of fleet

## Steps
1. Reserve static IP: `gcloud compute addresses create openchat-agent-ip --region=us-central1`
2. Provision: `gcloud compute instances create openchat-agent --zone=us-central1-a --machine-type=e2-micro --image-family=ubuntu-2404-lts-amd64 --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud --boot-disk-size=20GB --address=openchat-agent-ip --tags=https-server`
3. Bootstrap: install node 20, scp openchat-agent source up, npm ci --omit=dev, install systemd unit per README
4. .env contents: OPENCHAT_BOT_JWT (reuse picortex's), OPENCHAT_BASE_URL=https://chat.globalbr.ai, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (fresh, not picortex's), BOT_NAME=picortex (or whatever — keep mention trigger working)
5. Start service, verify in OpenChat: @ the bot in a test group, expect a reply
6. Observe for 48h
7. Stop picortex's OpenChat participation (kill openchat side of dispatcher only; leave Linq side running on picortex-v1 for now)
8. Decommission picortex-v1 GCP VM ~2 weeks after green status on openchat-agent

## Decision needed before step 4
- Bot identity: keep `picortex_bot_7ecd2883dbd5ceef` (preserves message history) or fresh `openchat_assistant_…` user (clean slate)?
- Bot display name: 'picortex' (existing mention trigger) or rename to something OpenChat-native ('OpenChat AI', 'Echo', etc.)?

## Acceptance
- openchat-agent VM running, systemd service active
- @mention in a group → reply within 5s
- picortex-v1 OpenChat side stopped, no double-reply
- 1 week of observation, no crashes
- docs/agent-integration-paths.md updated with the actual deployed state

## Dependencies
- OpenChat-p9y (the reconsideration decision) — implied resolved by Jacob if this ticket exists
- New ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for the shared bot (separate from picortex's, in case we need to revoke)
notes:
## Open decisions resolved 2026-06-01 (defaults — minimize change)

1. **Bot identity: keep `picortex_bot_7ecd2883dbd5ceef`.** Preserves every existing message authorship row in Neo4j; conversation memberships survive the swap; existing JWT minted off OpenChat's JWT_SECRET can be reused as-is (no JWT re-issue dance). Rename can come later if we ever want to.

2. **Bot display name: keep 'picortex'.** Existing @mention trigger keeps working — anyone in a group who's already typing '@picortex' doesn't need to relearn. The name baggage is real but doesn't block anything; we can do a name change separately as a one-shot Neo4j UPDATE once we feel like it.

Both choices = 'don't change things you don't need to change.' Step 4 of the deploy can copy picortex's .env values straight in (OPENCHAT_BOT_JWT, BOT_NAME=picortex). The only fresh secret is the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (so revoking it doesn't break picortex's Linq side during cutover).

title: Make /d/ installable as a PWA + landing page 'Install as app' CTA
description:
User feedback (2026-06-01): home page has no 'download desktop app' option. /d/ is currently just a browser tab — closes when browser closes, no dock icon, no OS push when browser focused elsewhere.

APPROACH: PWA (Progressive Web App). Make /d/ installable from Chrome / Edge / Brave / Safari Sonoma+ so users get:
- Own window (no browser chrome)
- Dock / taskbar icon
- OS-level notifications even when browser closed
- Auto-update for free (every server deploy = new version on next launch)

NOT building: Electron / Tauri / Mac Catalyst yet. Those are 4–10 hour projects with code-signing certs (/yr Apple + ~$200/yr Windows EV). PWA is 45 min, zero recurring cost. Revisit if PWA adoption suggests demand for a 'real' installer.

WORK:
1. Add /d/manifest.json with OpenChat icon, name, theme color, display:standalone, scope:/d/
2. Add a minimal service worker to /d/ (network-first; cache-app-shell-only — don't try to cache messages)
3. Inject <link rel='manifest'> into /d/ index.html (via expo web config or build-time post-processor)
4. Update landing page 'Desktop web' tile → 'Desktop · install as app' with subtitle 'Standalone window · OS notifications · works offline-first'
5. Add a small 'Install OpenChat' prompt on first /d/ visit (only show if browser supports beforeinstallprompt + user hasn't dismissed)

ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] Chrome on macOS shows 'Install OpenChat' button in URL bar at chat.globalbr.ai/d/
- [ ] After install, OpenChat appears in Applications with the correct icon
- [ ] Installed app opens in standalone window (no tabs/URL bar)
- [ ] Landing page tile updated to reflect the new install path

DEPENDENCY: blocked by OpenChat-601 (don't ship 'install this' for a broken app). Also coordinate with OpenChat-84u (homepage QR + deep-link share).

ESTIMATED EFFORT: 45 minutes.
close_reason: Shipped 2026-06-01: /d/ is now PWA-installable. Chrome/Edge/Brave show install button in URL bar; installed app gets its own window + dock icon + OS notifications. Landing page tile updated to 'Desktop · install as app'. Server smoke-tested: manifest, sw.js, icons, injected index.html tags all 200. Service worker is minimal (network-first, caches only app shell, never caches /api/ or /socket.io/) — safe default that doesn't risk stale message data.

title: Reconsider openchat-agent: shared-bot use case is distinct from MCP, not redundant
description:
Pulling this back out of 'archive' (OpenChat-do2) for reconsideration. OpenChat-fwi recommended archiving openchat-agent on the premise that openchat-mcp-server replaces it. That's wrong — they serve different use cases.

## What openchat-agent actually is
Headless Node service, ~300 LOC. NOT a cloud box. NOT a VM. Just code. Designed to ship as a systemd unit (`/opt/openchat-agent/`) or docker container, runs on any Linux host. Never deployed. Reuses (or replaces) picortex's bot JWT.

## Two distinct use cases — both legitimate
| Use case | Best path |
|---|---|
| 'MY agent reads MY chats' (single user, on-demand) | **MCP via per-user API key** |
| 'Shared assistant lives in our group, responds to @mentions, no per-user setup' | **openchat-agent (or picortex)** |

The MCP path requires every user to install Claude Desktop / Cursor / etc., mint a key, paste a config. Shared-bot path requires zero user setup — the bot just appears in the group and you @ it.

These are complementary, not competing.

## What needs to be answered
1. Do we want a shared OpenChat bot (vs. only per-user MCP)? If yes:
2. Should it be openchat-agent (slim, OpenChat-only) or keep picortex (already deployed)?
3. Where does it run? Options:
   - Co-host on picortex-v1 (cheap, defeats isolation)
   - testcortex (already there, but ⚠️ SECURITY — testcortex is on Tailscale; agent with shell-tool access could pivot — see ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md testcortex security section)
   - New GCP e2-micro ($5/mo, isolated)
   - Mac Mini (free, but Mac Mini has many other things)
   - Fly.io / Hetzner (cheap small VM)
4. Bot identity: keep picortex_bot or fresh user?
5. What about tools — should the shared bot have access to user-scoped operations? (probably not — least-privilege says shared bot can only do shared-conversation things)

## Decision needed before acting on OpenChat-do2
Until this ticket is resolved, DO NOT execute OpenChat-do2 (archive openchat-agent). If decision = 'no shared bot ever, MCP is enough', then OpenChat-do2 can proceed.

## Cross-references
- OpenChat-fwi (agent integration paths)
- OpenChat-do2 (archive openchat-agent — now BLOCKED on this)
- OpenChat-xem (picortex deprecation 2026-09-01 — may need adjustment if we keep the shared-bot path on openchat-agent)
- docs/agent-integration-paths.md (the design doc — needs an update reflecting this distinction)
close_reason: Resolved: openchat-agent stays, gets deployed (OpenChat-sju). Codex answer at /tmp/codex-agent-paths-review/ANSWER.md. Design doc updated.

description:
Main payoff of the consolidation — collapse the 3-way fork of the REST client and the message/conversation/agent-key types into shared workspace packages.

## Current state (the duplication we're killing)
- apps/web-legacy/src/api.ts (Vite client) — fetches + types
- apps/mobile/src/api/client.ts (RN client) — same shape, slightly different headers
- packages/mcp-server/src/api.ts (MCP adapter) — same again

## Target
- packages/shared-types/ — pure type-only package. Message, Conversation, Thought, AgentKey, User, etc.
- packages/api-client/ — fetch-based REST client that imports types from shared-types. Pluggable storage (SecureStore on RN, localStorage on web, env on Node). Mobile-friendly default.

## Steps
1. Extract types from one of the three sources (mobile is most complete) into packages/shared-types/
2. Build packages/api-client/ around fetch, with a small adapter interface for storage:
   ```ts
   interface TokenStorage {
     get(): Promise<string | null>;
     set(token: string): Promise<void>;
     clear(): Promise<void>;
   }
   ```
3. Replace the 3 forked clients with imports from @openchat/api-client. Each call site supplies its own TokenStorage instance.
4. Drop the now-dead files

## Acceptance
- All three apps build and type-check
- Server smoke test passes (deploy with packages/api-client used somewhere if applicable — actually the SERVER doesn't consume api-client, only the three CLIENTS do)
- No client code duplicates a fetch shape

title: [P2] OpenChat MCP server (sibling to wikihub-mcp-server)
description:
Build a thin MCP adapter over the OpenChat REST API so any MCP-aware client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Cline, etc.) can talk to OpenChat with one config snippet. Parallel to wikihub/mcp-server/ — same shape.

LOCATION: ~/code/openchat-mcp-server/ (new sibling repo, not in openchat or openchat-mobile)

TOOL SURFACE (initial):
- oc_list_conversations(): your conversations
- oc_get_messages(conversationId, limit?): recent messages
- oc_send_message(conversationId, text, attachments?): send (write)
- oc_react(messageId, emoji): tap-back
- oc_create_dm(userEmail): start a 1:1
- oc_register_agent(name, scopes?): mint a new key — uses caller's OAuth or JWT

TRANSPORT:
- stdio (for Claude Desktop)
- HTTP (for Cursor / hosted clients)

AUTH:
- Reads OPENCHAT_API_KEY env var OR Authorization: Bearer <key> header
- Falls back to credentials file ~/.openchat/credentials.json

DOCS:
- One-line install: 'npx -y @openchat/mcp-server' (publish to npm later)
- README with Claude Desktop config:
  {
    "mcpServers": {
      "openchat": {
        "command": "npx",
        "args": ["-y", "@openchat/mcp-server"],
        "env": { "OPENCHAT_API_KEY": "oc_…" }

title: [UX] Dark mode for OpenChat web app
description:
Add proper dark mode to OpenChat's web client. The app is currently bg-white / text-gray-900 across all surfaces — fine in daylight, harsh at night, and obviously not parity with the iMessage / WhatsApp / Telegram default that users expect.

## Approach
- Enable Tailwind dark mode: 'class' strategy in tailwind.config.js (not 'media' — we want user override, not system-only).
- Toggle in user menu (ChatSidebar's user dropdown): Light / Dark / System. Default 'System'.
- Persist choice in localStorage 'openchat_theme'. On boot, main.tsx applies the saved/derived class to <html>.
- React to system pref changes (matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').addEventListener) when in System mode.
- Update the existing <meta name='theme-color'> from #3b82f6 to also have a dark variant (use media-attribute form: <meta name='theme-color' content='#1e293b' media='(prefers-color-scheme: dark)'>) so the iOS Safari URL-bar tints correctly.
- Update manifest.webmanifest theme_color + background_color to have light/dark counterparts where browsers support it (only some do; safe to keep current light defaults).

## Files to audit for hardcoded colors
Every component that currently uses bg-white / bg-gray-50 / text-gray-* / border-gray-* needs dark: variants. Inventory from grep:
- client/src/pages/ChatPage.tsx (bg-gray-50 outer, header bg-white)
- client/src/components/ChatSidebar.tsx (bg-white, gray borders, status dropdown)
- client/src/components/ConversationList.tsx
- client/src/components/MessageList.tsx (bg-blue-500 own bubbles -> stays; bg-gray-100 other bubbles -> dark:bg-gray-700; text-gray-900 -> dark:text-gray-100)
- client/src/components/MessageInput.tsx (bg-white form, border-gray-200, border-gray-300 input)
- client/src/components/GroupSettings.tsx (modal bg-white)
- client/src/components/PresenceIndicator.tsx (presence dot colors — likely keep)
- client/src/components/InstallPrompt.tsx (sheet bg-white)
- client/src/App.tsx Toaster (already uses bg-red-100 / bg-green-100 — those work in both modes but darker variants would be cleaner)
- client/src/index.css base body bg
- The Noos feedback widget is 3rd-party; can't directly themed. data-theme='auto' is already set in index.html so it should respect prefers-color-scheme automatically.

## UX details
- Switch should be near-instant (no flash of unstyled content). Apply theme class BEFORE React mounts — in a small inline <script> in index.html that reads localStorage and applies the class to <html> synchronously.
- Bubble color choice for dark mode: own messages stay blue, others go to dark-gray (e.g. bg-slate-700). Sender-name labels go to slate-400.
- Status indicators (green/yellow/red/gray dots) stay the same vivid colors in both modes.
- Floating Noos widget data-theme='auto' should pick up the change.

## Acceptance
- Toggle in user menu works (Light / Dark / System).
- System mode tracks OS preference live (no reload needed).
- No flash of light theme on dark-mode-saved cold load.
- All conversation surfaces (list / chat / group settings modal / install prompt / login) look polished in dark.
- iOS Safari URL-bar tints with the theme.

## Phase
Phase 1 polish — chunky-but-not-blocking. Ship before declaring mobile UX 'done.' Roughly half a day of careful component-by-component audit + a couple of hours for the theme toggle infrastructure.

title: Sync SSO flow with Thoughtstreams / latest Noos pattern
description:
OpenChat SSO diverges from Thoughtstreams:

1. Thoughtstreams proxies /api/auth/sso-exchange through its own server; OpenChat calls Noos directly from the browser (cross-origin, requires CORS, leaks Noos URL, bakes in VITE_NOOS_URL at build time). Refactor OpenChat to POST to /api/auth/sso-exchange on its own server and have the server talk to Noos internally via NOOS_API_URL (already in docker-compose). Benefits: no cross-origin fetch, no VITE_NOOS_URL dependency for the exchange path, matches Thoughtstreams.

2. Thoughtstreams calls /auth/session-check on load to auto-resume a Noos session. OpenChat does not — users must click Continue with Noos even if already signed in on ts.globalbr.ai. Add session-check for true cross-app SSO.

3. Consider extracting a shared noos-sso npm module (used by OpenChat, Thoughtstreams, thoughtstream-gemini-jacob) so auth drift stops happening per-app. Tracked under noos-sso-ecosystem epic.
close_reason:
Obviated 2026-06-01 by /legacy/ deprecation (OpenChat-ixd default decision: don't invest in /legacy):

PART 1 (Vite client → server-proxy SSO exchange): The cross-origin sso-exchange call lives only in client/src/api.ts (the legacy Vite client). Per ixd, /legacy/ is deprecated; we're not investing in its refactors.

PART 2 (cross-app session-check on load): Could benefit /m/ and /d/ users coming from globalbr.ai. But requires Noos server cooperation and is genuinely separate work — file a new ticket if/when this becomes a priority.

PART 3 (shared noos-sso npm module): Belongs to the noos-sso-ecosystem epic, not OpenChat-scoped.

MOBILE (the canonical client now) does NOT have this divergence — it uses Google OAuth + Apple SIWA directly, no SSO-exchange round-trip. Verified via grep of openchat-mobile/src/ — zero matches for sso-exchange.

title: Explore expo-contacts integration + write tradeoffs
description:
Investigation only — produce a recommendation, do not implement.

QUESTION: Should OpenChat mobile request iOS Contacts access to power friend-discovery?

KEY FACTS:
- expo-contacts NOT installed
- iOS Contacts permission decline rate: 40-60% on cold prompts; 'Limited Access' further fragments matching
- WITHOUT phone-number sign-in, matching falls back to email — most iOS contacts don't have email — match rate ~5-10%

  3. Show matches with explicit 'Send invite' / 'Start chat' (no auto-friend)
  4. Server stores hashes only; no address-book copy

- [ ] If go-ahead: spawn implementation epic blocked-by phone-sign-in ticket

title: Decision: phone-number sign-in (WhatsApp-style)?
description:
DECISION ticket, not implementation. Decide whether/when to add SMS-OTP sign-in alongside Google OAuth.

CURRENT STATE: Google OAuth only (iOS + web). No phoneNumber field on :User. ~5 users.

TRADEOFF MATRIX:
| Dim                       | Google (today) | Phone+OTP                | Both                |
|---------------------------|----------------|--------------------------|---------------------|
| Onboarding friction       | Medium         | Low                      | Low                 |
| Cost                      | $0            | $0.005-0.04/SMS         | Marginal            |
| Dev/test                  | Easy           | Hard                     | Hard                |
| Abuse surface             | Low            | SIM swap, toll fraud     | Both                |
| Contacts matching         | Useless        | High value               | High value          |
| Portability               | Stable         | Numbers recycle          | Both                |
| iOS App Store             | Fine           | Triggers SIWA req        | SIWA req            |
| Time-to-ship              | N/A            | 1-2 weeks                | Same                |

RECOMMENDATION: DEFER. Stay Google-only for ~3 months. Revisit triggers:
  (a) >100 users AND contacts-matching is top growth lever, OR
  (b) Specific repeat user blocked by no-Google option.

WHEN BUILT: use Twilio Verify (not raw Programmable SMS) + add Sign in with Apple simultaneously (App Store rule). Design account-merge UX BEFORE first SMS goes out.

DO-NOW PREP (low effort, future-proofs):
- [ ] Add nullable phoneNumber (E.164) + phoneNumberVerifiedAt fields to :User in Neo4j (no migration needed)
- [ ] Add phoneNumberHash (sha256(E.164)) index

ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] Decision documented in resolution comment
- [ ] If 'defer': close with rationale + revisit-trigger; phoneNumber field added prophylactically
- [ ] If 'build now': spawn epic with sub-tickets for Twilio Verify wiring, SIWA, account-merge UX, abuse controls
close_reason: Decision shipped 2026-06-01 in docs/decisions/2026-06-01-phone-sign-in.md: DEFER phone-number sign-in.
